cs.t: I have used an Olympus E-P2 and Sony RX100.  These are good cameras, but not great, and not approaching a Leica M for one reason: the viewfinders (or lack thereof). An optical viewfinder is an essential feature which connects the shooter to the subject in a way that cannot be matched by an LCD.  And while the beloved Fuji X100(s) has an optical viewfinder, it has a pathetic 90% coverage and 0.5x magnification.  This makes a big, big difference in the active, engaged, photo-journalistic work that Leica is known for. For six years I shot with an Olympus E-1 DSLR.  It's lame by today's digital standards, with only 5MP, but it was far better as a tool for making images than any of these no-, small-, or electronic viewfinder cameras.
